symptom: `mxcli sql --alias shop --describe sales.customers` printed an empty column list and (0 rows), no error; `--describe customers` worked. --tables prints schema and table apart, so the qualified form is the natural next step.
file: sql/meta.go DescribeTable / columnsFilter / splitTableName / refuseAmbiguousTable. Test: sql/describe_qualified_2361_test.go (needs MXCLI_TEST_PG_DSN)
cause: The PostgreSQL and SQL Server templates compared table_name to the whole argument, so `sales.customers` matched no row; only the Oracle path split the schema off. An empty result was printed as a table with no columns.
insight: **Test the unverified case the reporter lists.** The unqualified form was the 'control', but on PostgreSQL 16 with `customers` in two schemas it returned both tables' columns as one (6 rows) — a second, silent defect. Measured: qualified now 3 columns; a missing table and an ambiguous name are errors that name the accepted form or the candidates; the revert gives 0 columns and no errors.
